summary: This pull request moves the question of what a deferral ships from the words of its mitigation to the round's own record, and takes deferrals out of the commit demand. The phrase list is gone, and the wording #100 pins no longer stops a round. The correctness findings are where a decided finding meets the new rules: a fix the person or autopilot decided can drop out of needCommits, through a reshape's re-sort (R1-10) or a stray filled entry beside an override (R1-11), and the plan approver's file-list rule reads the shaper's files where the workflow reads the resolve agent's (R1-2). The rest are a stop view that can go stale, docs and comments that say slightly more than the code does, and code this change left dead. There is no scheduled or queued work in this repository (no routes/console.php). The version moves to 0.4.1 as a patch, and the plan has a Docs entry for every touched file.

findings.title: Known limits does not say an uncounted mitigation commit goes unreviewed
findings.description: A deferral's mitigation commit is counted only if it is the finding's own (`ownCommit`, workflows/redline-loop.js:596-598): its subject opens `redline: <id>` or the implementer reported it for the finding. Otherwise `outcomesFor` zeroes it (2936-2938) and `fixed` leaves the finding out (4119). If nothing else in the round is fixed or bought, the run goes straight to the handoff. No final nit pass runs and no later round reads that code. Traced: a planned nit deferral (shaper files `['app/x.php']`) whose only commit is `redline: add a guard for R1-1 (#114)`, not reported for the finding. On this branch the reply is `deferred to #301.`, `fixed` is empty, `bought` is false, the run hands off and the planned-and-unbuilt warning fires. On main, `hasMitigation` was true, so the reply was `Mitigated in ...`, `fixed` held R1-1 and a final nit pass followed. README Known limits says such a commit `is not counted, so it is pushed with the round and named in no reply`. docs/running.md:125 says only that a counted commit `is reviewed like any fix`. Neither says the uncounted commit is read by no Redline pass. Conditions: the implementer departs from rule 3 of agents/redline-implementer.md twice (wrong subject and no report), and nothing else in the round earns a final nit pass or a re-review. If something does, the range the next pass reads runs from the previous head to the new one (4978), so it holds the commit anyway. shape.md records `not counted` as a change made on purpose; it does not mention the missing review. The repository's guard refuses `node` for the reviewer, so this was traced, not run. A harness that runs it against the branch and origin/main is at /tmp/redlinerepro/reviewer-r1-repro.mjs.
findings.proposedFix: Update README Known limits ("No commit is demanded of a deferral") and docs/running.md "Deferred items" (Whether a mitigation shipped) to add one clause: a commit that is not counted is read by no final nit pass or re-review unless something else in the round earns one.

findings.title: The approver's file-list bounce reads the shaper's files for a finding the person decided
findings.description:
Rule 1's new sentence makes it a bounce when a `defer` finding lists `files` with no task in `plan.md`, or has a task and lists none. The approver checks this against the findings planPrompt shows (workflows/redline-loop.js:2083). Those come from `effectiveDispositions()` (3838), which for a disposition override is the shaper's finding with only `disposition` replaced (3773-3776), so it keeps the shaper's `files`. The workflow itself never reads the shaper's list for a decided finding: it reads the resolve agent's tasks (`plannedFiles`, 3789-3791; `shaperPlanned` requires `!roundDecisions[id]`, 3785).

Two plan-dial paths meet the rule:
- A shaper fix (files listed) that the person changes to defer with nothing shipping. The resolve agent writes "no task when they name none" (2052), so the approver sees `"disposition": "defer"` with the fix's files and no task.
- A decline (`files: []`) overruled to defer with a mitigation that the resolve agent plans as a task. The approver sees a defer with a task and no files.

The rule calls both a bounce. A bounce runs a reshape (3857). The reshape prompt keeps a decision the person made "as it is" (2010), so a reshape that leaves that finding's files alone bounces again. After `maxPlanAdjustments` (2 by default, line 111) the round stops at approve (3853-3854).

Before this PR, rule 1 keyed on the mitigation ("A `defer` finding with an empty mitigation has no task, and that is no bounce"), so neither path bounced. Whether a given approver run bounces is that agent's call; its instructions tell it to.
findings.proposedFix: Show the approver the files the workflow reads. Either pass planPrompt each decided finding's resolve-task files (`plannedFiles`) in place of the shaper's `files`, or say in rule 1 that for a finding the prompt's decisions list, the resolve agent's task decides and the shaper's `files` are not read.

findings.title: Stray space before a comma in the plan dial's field list
findings.description: This PR's edit to the plan-dial paragraph left `(the sentence Redline will post in the finding's thread) , \`decidedBy\``, with a space before the comma. The base branch read `... thread) and \`decidedBy\``.
findings.proposedFix: Write `(the sentence Redline will post in the finding's thread), \`decidedBy\``.

findings.title: The unattended section's return example omits the now-required `files`
findings.proposedFix: Add `files` to every finding in the example in templates/shape-spec-unattended.md, matching agents/redline-shaper.md, and to the sentence at line 97, with the template marker and minor bump the release standard asks for. Otherwise, record in the spec why the example stays as it is.

findings.title: New module-level `filled(item)` is shadowed by a local `filled(s)`
findings.description: The new module-level `filled(item)` (783) takes a deferred entry and reads `item.mitigation`. The coverage parser declares its own `const filled = (s) => typeof s === 'string' && s.trim() !== ''` (1717-1718), which takes a string and shadows the module-level one inside that block. Neither block calls the other's helper today. An edit near 1717 that means the entry helper would get the string one, and `filled(entry)` would return false for every entry.
findings.proposedFix: Rename the module-level helper, for example `mitigationFilled`, at its one call in isDeferral (3806).

findings.title: The deferred outcome's mitigation fallbacks can no longer run
findings.description: `shipsNothing` is now true whenever no commit of the finding's own landed (2936-2937), and `own` is a subset of `named`. So a deferred outcome either has commits (`shipped = named`, non-empty) or has `mitigation: ''` (2954). The fallback branches `outcome.mitigation ? ' Mitigation: ...'` in replyBody (1523) and `; mitigation: ...` in describeOutcome (2993) can never run. Deferred outcomes are only built at 2954 and copied with their commits at 3467. Those two branches are the only readers of the outcome's `mitigation` field. Before this PR they ran for a deferral whose words read as a mitigation and that had no commit.
findings.proposedFix: Remove the two fallback branches (1523, 2993) and the deferred outcome's `mitigation` field (2954).

findings.title: A mitigation's words are hidden whenever the record says nothing ships, contrary to the comment and the docs
findings.description:
`draftView` sets `mitigation: ships ? d.item.mitigation : ''` (3407), and `deferredEntry` keeps the words only when the outcome has commits (3387). So the words are blanked exactly when the record says nothing ships.

The new comment at 777-779 says the opposite: "The words are shown, at a stop and in the result, beside what the record says". docs/running.md:125 says the same ("the words of the mitigation, which are only shown"), and shape.md decision 1 says "The words are kept for display." draftView's own comment (3404) and the skill (skills/redline/SKILL.md:217, `empty when nothing ships`) describe what the code does.

The effect shows when the shaper writes a mitigation and a plan task but lists no `files`, the case the second warning (4044) exists for. The first stop (3684-3686) runs before any plan approver and shows `ships: false`, `mitigation: ''`, `files: []`, so the person sees no sign that a mitigation was written. The build can still commit it, and it is posted as mitigated; the only notice is the warning in the run's result.
findings.proposedFix: Either show the words at the stop whatever `ships` says, with the skill saying how to present `ships: false` beside written words, or correct the comment at 777-779 and docs/running.md:125 to say the words are shown only beside a mitigation that ships.

findings.title: draftsOf's default parameter names a const declared about 150 lines later
findings.proposedFix: Drop the default and pass the files reader at every call: `draftsOf(list, shaperFiles)` at 3653, `draftsOf(list, plannedFiles)` at 3814 and 4022.

findings.title: A draft's version ignores the `ships` and `files` the stop now shows, so an answered draft is not raised again when they change
findings.description:
A draft's version only counts changes to the issue text (3641-3646). issueDraft (1318-1330) holds the title, found, file and line, why and fullFix, and an answer covers every version up to the one it named (`draftAnswered`, 219). The stop now also shows `ships` and `files` (3405-3407): from the shaper's list at the first stop (3653), and from `plannedFiles` after the round's decisions. A reshape that changes a deferral's `files` but not its draft leaves the version unchanged, so `draftStop` after the reshape (3882) raises nothing. A person who answered Go ahead on `ships: false` is never shown that a mitigation now ships, and the build commits it with the reply `Mitigated in ...`.

The new approver rule (agents/redline-plan-approver.md:16) bounces exactly this mismatch (a deferral with a task in plan.md and no `files`), and a reshape that fixes the list is the expected outcome.

Traced on the guided dial:
1. The shaper defers R1-1 with a plan task, mitigation words and `files: []`.
2. The first stop shows `ships: false` and `mitigation: ''`.
3. The relaunch answers Go ahead for version 1.
4. The approver bounces, and the reshape lists `['app/x.php']`.
5. The draft text is unchanged, so version 1 still counts as answered.
6. The implementer commits `redline: R1-1 ...`, the outcome has its own commit, and it is posted as mitigated with no warning.

The version never covered the mitigation's words either, so a reshape that rewrote the words had the same gap on main. What this PR adds is `ships`/`files` on the stop and the bounce that changes them. Conditions: a shaper that lists no files for a planned mitigation (or lists files for none), a dial that raises drafts, and a reshape that corrects the list. Traced, not run; the harness is at /tmp/redlinerepro/reviewer-r1-repro.mjs (c5c6).
findings.proposedFix: Count the version over what the stop shows: include `ships`, the files and the mitigation words in the text compared at 3644, or keep a second fingerprint of them beside `text` and bump the version when it changes. Add a loop check: answer version 1 at a stop that shows `ships: false`, bounce, have the reshape list files, and expect a second stop.

findings.title: deferralIds counts a decided call that a reshape re-sorted to defer, so its planned fix is no longer demanded
findings.description:
`deferralIds` joins `finalDispositions.filter(defer)` to `deferred.filter(isDeferral)` (3949). The candidate reads the second list as already held in the first. It is not, and the difference is a lost commit demand.

How it happens:
- A judgment call's decision carries no `disposition` (autopilotDecision, 1364-1371; a person's answer to a call likewise).
- So `effectiveDispositions` gives such a finding whatever disposition a reshape returned (3773-3776).
- Suppose a reshape after a bounce sorts a decided call's finding as `defer` (the #97 R1-10 case; scenario strayReshape at tests/loop-test.mjs:3093).
- isDeferral says it is not a deferral (3804-3806). The reshape's entry is dropped as restated (3874-3879), so `resolveDeferred` never holds it.
- But `finalDispositions` says defer, so `deferralIds` holds it, and the resolve task that the person's answer planned is dropped from `needCommits` (3953).

Traced with strayReshape's scenario and no commit (`commitIds [[], []]`). On this branch the check passes with no repair and no warning: the finding is not in `roundDeferrals` (4022), so neither warning at 4036-4045 fires. The reply is `Redline round 1: Fix it now. No code change. · decided by: @author`. On main, the resolve-task clause demanded the task's commit (removed line `.concat(resolvedTasks.filter((task) => task.files.length && task.finding && !accepted.has(task.finding) && !record.forced[task.finding]).map((task) => task.finding))`, which had no deferral exclusion), and the round stopped at the check after its repair.

The candidate's other point holds: `deferred.filter(isDeferral)` is computed three times (3949, 4022, 4030), and each isDeferral call rebuilds `effectiveDispositions()`.

Conditions: a reshape that re-sorts a decided call to defer, and an implementer that skips that call's task. Traced, not run, since the guard refuses `node` to the reviewer; the harness at /tmp/redlinerepro/reviewer-r1-repro.mjs (c11) runs both branches.
findings.proposedFix: Build `deferralIds` from `deferred.filter(isDeferral)` alone. Compute it once after the build (`const roundDeferred = deferred.filter(isDeferral)`) and reuse it at 4022 and 4030. Add a loop check: strayReshape with `commitIds [[], []]` stops at the check with `no commit names R1-1`.

findings.title: A person's override to fix is no longer demanded when the resolve agent returns a filled entry for it
findings.description:
`needCommits` now leaves out every id in `deferralIds` (3949-3953). For a disposition override to `fix` (plan dial, decision `{disposition: 'fix'}`), isDeferral still returns true when the resolve agent's entry for the finding has a filled mitigation, even though the decision names `fix`. The test is `decision.disposition === 'defer' || (resolveDeferred.has(d.id) && (filled(d) || ...))` (3804-3806).

Traced: the shaper defers R1-1, the person overrides it to fix, and the resolve agent plans the fix's task but also returns `{mitigation: 'a guard', ...draft}`. The build leaves the fix out.
- `awayFromDefer` drops the shaper's entry (3727) and the resolve agent's entry is added (3766-3769).
- isDeferral is true, so `deferralIds` is {R1-1}, `needCommits` is empty, and the check passes with no repair.
- The draft is filed as #301 (4025-4028), and the outcome is decided with no commits (2948).
- The reply is `Redline round 1: Fix it in full. No code change. Deferred to #301. · decided by: @author`.
- The warning `round 1: R1-1 planned a mitigation in app/x.php and no commit of its own landed; posted as shipping nothing` fires, where app/x.php is the fix's task (`plannedFiles` reads `resolvedTasks`, 3789-3790).

On main the same entry was already read as a deferral (`hasMitigation`), but `needCommits` demanded the fix by its final disposition (removed line `.filter((f) => f.disposition === 'fix' || (f.disposition === 'defer' && mitigated(f.id)))`), so the round stopped at the check after its repair. On the guided and plan dials the person sees the stray draft at the stop after the resolve (`draftStop`, 3813-3828) and can drop it, but no answer there restores the demand. A bounce would drop the stray entry (`awayFromDefer` at 3879), so this needs a plan approved first time.

#99 tracks a stray entry beside a judgment call answered with a fix, and the comment this PR drafted for #99 (shape.md, "For you to add to #99") says a fix read as a deferral through a stray filled entry is no longer demanded. #99 does not cover the override case, and an override needs none of the new resolve-agent field #99 proposes: the decision already carries `disposition: 'fix'`, which isDeferral only reads when it is `defer`.

Conditions: the resolve agent returns a filled entry with a full draft for an override to fix. The override block of the resolve prompt (2052) does not forbid this; the "only when its decision defers" sentence (2046) covers calls only. Traced, not run; the harness is at /tmp/redlinerepro/reviewer-r1-repro.mjs (c1).
findings.proposedFix: In isDeferral, return false for a decision whose `disposition` is set and is not `defer` (an explicit override), before reading the entry. Alternatively, keep `needCommits` demanding every final `fix` and every resolve task of a decision whose disposition is `fix`. Add a loop check: the plan-dial override to fix with a stray `{mitigation: 'a guard'}` entry and no commit stops at the check with `no commit names R1-1` and files nothing.

findings.title: The decided form of the "commit of its own" warning is pinned by no check and described by no doc
findings.description:
The second warning has two texts (4044):
- for a finding the person or autopilot decided: `the resolve agent planned no task with files for it; posted with its decision`;
- otherwise: `the shaper listed no files for its task; posted as its mitigation`.

tests/loop-test.mjs pins only the shaper's text (2907). A search of tests/, docs/, README.md and skills/ finds the decided text nowhere, and docs/running.md:125 and the PR description list only the shaper's. A change to the decided branch stays green, and a person reading the run's result meets a warning the docs do not describe.
findings.proposedFix: Add a loop check: a call answered "Mitigate" whose resolve agent plans no task with files (`acceptedCalls`) and whose commit is the finding's own (`commitIds [['R1-1']]`), expecting the decided text. Name that text in docs/running.md, "Deferred items", Whether a mitigation shipped.

accounting.ref: #99: a stray resolve entry beside a call answered with a fix is filed as the person's deferral. This pull request records the `none` case as a deliberate change (shape.md decision 14 and "Behaviour that changes on purpose"), pins it as intended in tests/loop-test.mjs:3088 (strayWorded), and drafts a comment on #99 about the commit demand it no longer makes.

list.summary: needCommits now leaves out a final `fix` whenever isDeferral reads it as a deferral, so a person's explicit `fix` override with a stray filled resolve entry is no longer demanded. Partly tracked in #99: for an override the disposition is already in roundDecisions, so isDeferral (line 3806) could read it directly without waiting for #99.
list.failure_scenario: Plan dial: the shaper defers R1-1 and the person overrides it to {disposition: 'fix'}. The resolve agent also returns a stray entry {mitigation: 'a guard'} and the fix is never built. Reproduced: main stops at the check with `no commit names R1-1` after its repair. This branch ends `done` with no repair, files issue #301, and posts `Fix it in full. No code change. Deferred to #301.` The warning wrongly says `R1-1 planned a mitigation in app/x.php`. The person's explicit fix is silently turned into a filed deferral.

list.summary: The new bounce rule (a `defer` that lists `files` with no task, or a task with no `files`, is a bounce) is checked against effectiveDispositions(). That function keeps the shaper's original `files` for a disposition override, while the workflow reads a decided finding's plan from the resolve agent's tasks (the R2-6 split).
list.failure_scenario: The person overrides the shaper's fix R1-1 (files ['app/x.php']) to defer with nothing shipping. The resolve agent plans no task, but the approver prompt shows `"disposition": "defer" ... "files": ["app/x.php"]` (confirmed in the planPrompt JSON). Rule 1 bounces it. The reverse also bounces: a decline overruled to defer-with-mitigation has shaper files [] and a resolve task. Each bounce costs a reshape, and if the reshape keeps the list the round stops at `approve` after maxPlanAdjustments.

list.summary: A deferral's commit that only mentions its id is now zeroed, so it drops out of `fixed` and `bought`: such a mitigation is pushed but read by no final nit pass and no re-review. The spec accepts that it is not counted; it does not say it also goes unreviewed, and neither README Known limits nor docs/running.md says so.
list.failure_scenario: Nit deferral R1-1 with a planned task, committed as `redline: add a guard for R1-1 (#114)` and not claimed by an implementer report (e.g. a sha shorter than 7). Reproduced: main ran `pr,final-nit-pass` and replied `Mitigated in 1bbbbbb`. This branch runs `pr` only, hands off, and replies `deferred to #301.` New code ships to the teammate with no Redline review, under a warning that says `posted as shipping nothing`.

list.summary: isDeferral now treats any filled mitigation as the person's deferral, so a stray resolve entry worded `none` or `n/a` beside a call planned as a fix files a GitHub issue, and the fix's commit drops out of needCommits. Already tracked in #99, whose posted comment covers this; tests/loop-test.mjs:3088 (strayWorded) pins it as intended.
list.failure_scenario: Autopilot answers call R1-1 with a full fix. The resolve agent also returns {mitigation: 'none'}. Before, the phrase list read it as empty: not a deferral, fix demanded, no issue. Now issue #301 is opened for a finding that was fixed, and if the fix's task is skipped the check passes with a warning.

list.summary: draftView and deferredEntry (line 3387) blank the mitigation words whenever the record says nothing ships. This hides exactly the case where the words and the record disagree. The comment at line 777 claims the words are 'shown, at a stop and in the result, beside what the record says'.
list.failure_scenario: The shaper defers R1-1 with mitigation 'Log the retry count' and writes the task in plan.md, but returns files [] (as the template example in templates/shape-spec-unattended.md does). The first stop runs before any plan approver and shows ships:false with mitigation '' and files [], so the person answers on 'nothing ships'. The implementer then builds and commits it, and it is posted as mitigated.

list.summary: A draft's version is counted over the issue text only, but the stop now shows `ships` and `files` from the plan. A reshape that changes a deferral's files never re-raises a draft that was already answered, and the new approver rule is what triggers such reshapes.
list.failure_scenario: At the first stop the person sees R1-1 with ships:false and answers Go ahead. The approver then bounces 'lists no files but plan.md has a task', and the reshape lists ['app/x.php']. The draft text is unchanged, so version 1 still counts as answered. The person is never told that a mitigation now ships, and it is committed and pushed.

list.summary: The unattended section's return example, which the shaper reads in every repository, shows no `files` on any finding, including the deferral R1-4 whose mitigation ships. The schema now requires `files`, and shaperPlanned and the stop read it. The spec kept the template unchanged because its prose stays true; the example JSON is what now contradicts the schema and agents/redline-shaper.md.
list.failure_scenario: A shaper following the template example puts files: [] on a deferral that has a mitigation task. The stop says nothing ships (above), the approver bounces, and if the build lands it anyway the run raises the 'shaper listed no files' warning. The cost is an extra reshape or a misleading stop on every repository set up from the template.

list.summary: The decided variant of the second warning ('the resolve agent planned no task with files for it; posted with its decision') is pinned by no loop check. docs/running.md 'Whether a mitigation shipped' lists only the shaper variant.
list.failure_scenario: Rewording or removing the decided branch of the ternary stays green, and a person reading the run's result finds a warning text the docs do not describe.

list.summary: The `outcome.mitigation ? ' Mitigation: ...'` branches in replyBody (line 1523) and describeOutcome (line 2993) can no longer run, and the deferred outcome's `mitigation` field (line 2954) is read only by them.
list.failure_scenario: shipsNothing is false only when there is a commit of the finding's own, and then `commits` is non-empty. So a deferred outcome with no commits always has mitigation ''. The dead fallback suggests a reply path ('Mitigation: <words>') that #100 removed; delete both branches and the field.

list.summary: draftsOf's default parameter `filesOf = plannedFiles` refers to a `const` declared about 150 lines later (line 3789). Any call without the second argument before that line throws a temporal-dead-zone ReferenceError.
list.failure_scenario: Today only shaperDrafts (line 3653) calls it early, and it passes shaperFiles. A future stop that calls draftsOf(list) before line 3789, or a reorder of these declarations, crashes the round with `Cannot access 'plannedFiles' before initialization`. Declare plannedTask, shaperPlanned and plannedFiles above draftsOf, or pass the reader explicitly.

list.summary: deferralIds concatenates `finalDispositions.filter(defer)` onto `deferred.filter(isDeferral)`, which already contains them. `deferred.filter(isDeferral)` is also recomputed at lines 3949, 4022 and 4030, and each isDeferral call rebuilds effectiveDispositions().
list.failure_scenario: Wasted O(n²) work, and three copies of one list that must stay in step. Compute `const roundDeferred = deferred.filter(isDeferral)` once after the build and reuse it for deferralIds, roundDeferrals and outcomesFor.

list.summary: The new module-level `filled(item)`, which takes a deferred entry, is shadowed by a local `filled(s)`, which takes a string, inside the coverage parser at line 1717.
list.failure_scenario: Two helpers with the same name and different argument types: a later edit near line 1717 that means the module-level one gets the string version. Rename one (e.g. `mitigationFilled`) or build the item check on a shared string helper.
